layers.authority: Cliffs of Moher Experience (visitor attraction on the Clare coast)
layers.process: Admission is charged and a booking buys a 2-hour visit from the entry time. Online rates listed for 2027: adult EUR 14 at peak (about A$22.25), EUR 9 off-peak (A$14.30), EUR 7 late evening in summer (A$11.12); family EUR 28 peak. Gate rates without booking: adult EUR 15 in 2026 and EUR 16 in 2027 (about A$25.42, RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293). Children under 12 are free with a parent or guardian (up to 4). Coach groups of 10 or more book through the groups department.

laws.rule: Cliffs of Moher: dogs must stay on leads and are not allowed in the visitor centre unless they are registered guide or support dogs.

Clare County Council Beach Bye-Laws 2021 apply year round to the scheduled beaches mapped in Schedule 3, including Fanore, Lehinch, Spanish Point, Doolin, White Strand at Miltown, Quilty, Seafield, Doughmore, Carrigaholt, Kilkee, Cappagh, and the lake beaches at Mountshannon, Ballycuggaran (Killaloe) and Ballyallia. On those beaches it is forbidden to light an open fire (other than in a contained unit such as a barbecue), damage dunes or plants, remove sand, stones, seaweed or soil without consent, drive or park a motor vehicle, camper, quad bike or similar on the beach or dunes (except when launching or retrieving a craft at a designated launch area), or camp or erect a tent, caravan or campervan. The vehicle ban at Spanish Point does not apply during the Willie Clancy Festival each year. Selling, hiring or offering tuition needs a council licence. During the summer season (15 May to 15 September) horses and dogs must not be brought onto a scheduled beach between 11 am and 6 pm, except at Doughmore where they are allowed at all times if kept under control (dogs on a leash) and faeces are removed; horses must stay off the dunes. Launching or using personal watercraft, power craft or fast power craft is prohibited except at designated areas, is prohibited from Lahinch beach, and personal watercraft must not be launched or used at Ballyallia Lake. Use of those craft within 300 metres of the low water mark is prohibited except for rescue or designated access, and speed is limited to 6 knots out to 300 metres. Inflatable toys must not be used on the water. Surfboards, sailboards, kiteboards, canoes, kayaks and stand-up paddle boards must not be used close to swimmers or in a designated bathing area. Commercial filming needs council consent. A person who contravenes the bye-laws is liable to an on-the-spot fine of EUR 75 (about A$119 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293), or to a fine not exceeding EUR 1,904.60 (about A$3,027) on summary conviction, and EUR 126.97 (about A$202) for each day a contravention continues after conviction.
